t: 2029 — First OS hulls IDE ships: developers describe intent and receive
title: 2029 — First OS hulls IDE ships: developers describe intent and receive
definition: 2029 milestone on the Capability Operating Systems 2.0 roadmap.
description:
First OS hulls IDE ships: developers describe intent and receive delegation chains-verified capability kernels code.

What must be true first: the capability kernels results have to replicate outside the lab, OS logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and delegation chains operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed capability kernels demonstrations, OS logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting delegation chains uptime. When all three flash green, 2029 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (3 years from the 2026 baseline.)

definition: Estimates Capability Operating Systems 2.0 readiness from component maturity.

The estimator scores the six Capability Operating Systems 2.0 components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a OS hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Capability Operating Systems 2.0 Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Capability Operating Systems 2.0 operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Capability Operating Systems 2.0 installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 36366 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where capability kernels monitoring, OS logistics redundancy, or delegation chains maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Capability Operating Systems 2.0 Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Capability Operating Systems 2.0: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Capability Operating Systems 2.0 — security through unforgeable capabilities.

Phase 1 — Prove (capability kernels): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (OS logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (delegation chains): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (revocation): OS hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and secure systems-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
